examples.en: They say Jumong founded Goguryeo.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 백 년 전에 건국했어요.
examples.en: That country was founded a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 나라를 건국한 왕의 이야기가 드라마로 나왔어요.
examples.en: A drama came out about the king who founded the country.
People who wanted to found a new country gathered.
Many things happened in the process of founding the country.
It is a country that was founded and has continued until now.

explain: 나라를 처음 세울 때만 쓰고, 회사나 학교를 세울 때는 '설립하다', '세우다'를 써요. 주어는 보통 사람이나 왕이에요. 나라가 주어일 때는 '건국되다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is only for founding a country; for companies or schools, use '설립하다' or '세우다'. The subject is usually a person or a king. When the country is the subject, '건국되다' is more common.

examples.ko: 정부는 경제 난국을 풀기 위해 노력하고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is working hard to resolve the economic crisis.

examples.ko: 회사가 난국에 빠졌지만 모두 힘을 모았어요.
examples.en: The company fell into a crisis, but everyone pulled together.
As the crisis drags on, the employees are getting worn out too.

examples.ko: 지금의 난국은 하루아침에 생긴 게 아니에요.
examples.en: The current crisis didn't appear overnight.

examples.ko: 난국 속에서도 그는 침착함을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even in the crisis, he stayed calm.
The worse the crisis, the more a leader's words matter.

explain: 정치, 경제, 회사처럼 큰 일의 어려운 상황에 써요. 개인의 일에는 '위기'나 '곤경'이 더 자연스러워요. '난국을 타개하다', '난국을 극복하다'처럼 같이 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used for difficult situations in big matters like politics, the economy or a company. For personal problems, '위기' or '곤경' sounds more natural. It often pairs with '타개하다' and '극복하다', as in '난국을 타개하다'.

examples.ko: 그동안 숨겨 온 거짓말이 만천하에 드러났어요.
examples.en: The lie that had been hidden all this time was revealed to everyone.

examples.ko: 기자가 이 사실을 만천하에 알리겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: The reporter said he would let the whole world know this fact.
I made a promise in front of the whole world.

examples.ko: 만천하의 눈이 이 재판에 쏠려 있어요.
examples.en: All eyes are on this trial.

examples.ko: 비밀이 만천하에 공개돼 회사가 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
examples.en: The secret was made public, and the company was thrown into an uproar.

examples.ko: 부끄러운 일이 만천하에 알려질까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried that something embarrassing will become known to everyone.

explain: '만천하에 알리다, 드러나다, 공개되다'처럼 쓰고, 숨기던 일이 모든 사람에게 알려진다는 느낌이에요. 보통 조사 '에'와 함께 나오고 뉴스나 연설에서 자주 들려요. 일상에서는 '다 알게 되다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '만천하에 알리다', '드러나다' and '공개되다', carrying the feeling that something hidden becomes known to everyone. It usually comes with the particle '에' and is often heard in news and speeches. In daily talk people say '다 알게 되다'.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 백 년 전에 설립됐어요.
examples.en: This school was founded a hundred years ago.
A new company is being established in Seoul.
Once the foundation is established, it will give scholarships.
It's a publishing company founded in 1990.
I covered the process of the institute being established.

examples.ko: 아직 설립되지 않은 단체라서 이름이 없어요.
examples.en: It's an organization not yet established, so it has no name.

explain: 회사, 학교, 단체, 재단처럼 조직을 세워 만드는 일에 써요. 건물을 짓는 것은 '세워지다/지어지다'라서 구분돼요. 회사 소개에서 '○○년에 설립된'이라는 말이 아주 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Used for organizations like companies, schools, groups, and foundations being set up. A building being put up is 세워지다 or 지어지다, so they differ. In company intros, the phrase '○○년에 설립된' appears constantly.

p.n: 신설되다 stresses that something new was set up; 설립되다 is the usual word for founding an organization.

examples.ko: 그는 사기죄로 삼 년 동안 수감됐어요.
examples.en: He was imprisoned for three years for fraud.

examples.ko: 수감된 사람도 가족과 편지를 주고받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even inmates can exchange letters with their families.

examples.ko: 형이 수감되는 날 가족들이 모두 울었어요.
examples.en: The whole family cried on the day my brother was imprisoned.
Before he was imprisoned, he was an ordinary office worker.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 지금 교도소에 수감돼 있어요.
examples.en: He is currently held in prison.

examples.ko: 곧 수감될 거라는 소식을 들었지만 믿을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I heard he would soon be jailed, but I couldn't believe it.

explain: '감옥에 가다'보다 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 가두는 쪽은 '수감하다', 들어가는 쪽은 '수감되다'이고, 보통 '교도소에 수감되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '감옥에 가다' and is used in news and legal talk. The side that locks someone up uses '수감하다', the one who goes in uses '수감되다', as in '교도소에 수감되다'.

examples.en: On Memorial Day, events honoring the patriotic martyrs are held.

examples.ko: 순국선열의 희생 덕분에 우리가 자유를 누려요.
examples.en: We enjoy freedom thanks to the sacrifice of the patriotic martyrs.

examples.ko: 학생들이 순국선열 묘역을 찾아 꽃을 놓았어요.
examples.en: The students visited the martyrs' cemetery and laid flowers.
Everyone observed a moment of silence for the patriotic martyrs.
I saw the belongings of the patriotic martyrs in person at the museum.

examples.ko: 순국선열 이야기를 읽고 많은 것을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I felt a lot after reading the stories of the patriotic martyrs.

explain: 나라를 위해 목숨을 바친 분들을 높여 부르는 말이에요. 현충일이나 기념식 같은 행사와 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, '순국선열께'처럼 높임을 담아 말해요.
explain_en: It is a respectful term for people who gave their lives for their country. It often appears around Memorial Day, ceremonies and the news, and is addressed with honorifics, as in '순국선열께'.

examples.en: The company tried to hush up the accident.
It was embarrassing, so the family kept it quiet among themselves.
Hushing up a problem doesn't solve it.
Everyone knew, but the mood was to keep quiet about it.
Even if you hush it up, rumors spread quickly.
Please don't just hush that matter up and move on.

explain: 나쁜 일이나 잘못이 밖으로 알려지지 않게 조용히 덮을 때 써요. 대부분 비판하는 느낌이 있어요. 한 사람이 숨기는 것보다 여러 사람이 입을 닫는 장면에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when a bad thing or a mistake is quietly covered up so it doesn't get out. It usually carries a note of criticism. It fits scenes where several people keep their mouths shut better than one person hiding something.

examples.en: The criminal confessed everything at the police station.
If you confess your wrongdoing, your mind feels at ease.
He admitted his lie and apologized.
Some people never confess to the end.
The child confesses to having broken the window.
I didn't have the courage to confess, so I kept hiding it.

explain: '고백하다'는 사랑이나 비밀 같은 마음을 말할 때도 쓰지만, '자백하다'는 자기가 한 나쁜 일이나 죄만 말할 때 써요. 가벼운 잘못에는 '털어놓다'나 '실토하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '고백하다' can be used for love or secrets, but '자백하다' is only for admitting your own wrongdoing or crime. For minor faults, '털어놓다' or '실토하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The soldiers arm themselves heavily with guns and body armor.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 모자와 장갑으로 중무장하고 나가요.
examples.en: On cold days I go out fully bundled up with a hat and gloves.

examples.ko: 중무장한 경비원이 은행 앞에 서 있어요.
examples.en: A heavily armed guard is standing in front of the bank.

examples.ko: 겨울 산에 갈 때는 단단히 중무장해야 해요.
examples.en: When you go up a mountain in winter, you have to gear up properly.

examples.ko: 아이는 우산과 장화로 중무장하고 비 오는 길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: The child, fully equipped with an umbrella and rain boots, walked down the rainy road.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에는 커피와 간식으로 중무장하고 도서관에 가요.
examples.en: During exams I go to the library stocked up with coffee and snacks.

explain: 군대 이야기 말고도 옷이나 장비를 잔뜩 갖추고 나설 때 가볍게 써요. 반대로 간단하게 갖추는 건 '경무장하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Besides military talk, it is used lightly when someone sets out with lots of clothes or gear. The opposite, equipping lightly, is '경무장하다'.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 전쟁이 나자 징병을 시작했어요.
examples.en: That country started a draft when the war broke out.
Draft notices arrived for the young men.
Many families were separated because of conscription.

examples.ko: 징병을 피하려고 외국으로 떠난 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: There are people who left for other countries to avoid the draft.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 징병과 모병의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned the difference between conscription and volunteer recruitment.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 징병 연령을 낮추는 문제를 다루고 있어요.
examples.en: The news is covering the issue of lowering the draft age.

explain: '입대'는 군대에 들어가는 사람 쪽에서, '징병'은 나라가 사람을 불러 모으는 쪽에서 하는 말이에요. 반대로 스스로 지원해서 군인을 모으는 건 '모병'이라고 해요. 일상에서는 '군대에 가다'라고 하고, '징병'은 뉴스나 역사 수업에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '입대' is said from the viewpoint of the person joining the military, while '징병' is from the viewpoint of the state calling people up. The opposite, recruiting volunteers, is '모병'. In daily talk people say '군대에 가다', and '징병' appears mostly in news and history lessons.

examples.en: The police arrested the thief.

examples.ko: 경찰은 그 남자를 곧 체포할 거예요.
examples.en: The police will arrest that man soon.
I watched a movie about arresting a criminal.
They took the arrested person to the police station.

examples.ko: 경찰이 길에서 그 사람을 체포하고 이름을 물었어요.
examples.en: The police arrested him on the street and asked his name.

examples.ko: 아직 체포하지 못해서 계속 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: They have not been able to arrest him yet, so they keep looking.

explain: '잡다'는 누구나 쓰지만 '체포하다'는 경찰이나 수사 기관이 할 때만 써요. 친구를 붙잡았을 때는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스에서는 '검거하다'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 경찰 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: Anyone can use '잡다', but '체포하다' is only for police or investigators. You would not use it when you grab a friend. In the news, '검거하다' is used similarly, but it is the police's own word.

examples.en: The police questioned the suspect all night.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 형사가 취조하는 장면이 인상 깊었어요.
examples.en: The scene in the drama where the detective interrogates someone was impressive.
Please don't ask me as if you're interrogating me to tell the truth.

examples.ko: 친구가 어제 어디 갔냐고 저를 취조해요.
examples.en: My friend grills me about where I went yesterday.

examples.ko: 취조받는 사람도 변호사를 부를 수 있어요.
examples.en: A person being interrogated can also call a lawyer.

examples.ko: 엄마가 성적표를 보고 저를 취조하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My mom looked at my report card and started grilling me.

explain: 경찰이나 검사가 혐의가 있는 사람에게 꼬치꼬치 캐묻는 장면에서 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서는 친구나 가족이 집요하게 물어볼 때 '취조하는 것 같다'고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요. 수사 뉴스에서는 '조사하다'라는 말도 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is used for scenes where police or prosecutors press a suspect with detailed questions. In daily life people jokingly say '취조하는 것 같다' when a friend or family member keeps asking pushy questions. In investigation news, '조사하다' is also used.

examples.en: In the old days, foreign enemies often invaded our country.

examples.ko: 적이 침략해 오자 사람들은 성으로 피했어요.
examples.en: When the enemy invaded, people took refuge in the castle.
In the movie, aliens invade Earth.

examples.ko: 다른 나라를 침략하는 것은 국제법 위반이에요.
examples.en: Invading another country violates international law.
It came out that they had made plans to invade.
That region was invaded several times.

explain: 다른 나라를 힘으로 공격해 들어가는 나쁜 일에 써요. 남의 집이나 건물에 몰래 들어가는 것은 '침입하다'예요. 공격을 받은 쪽은 '침략을 당하다', '침략당하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It describes attacking and entering another country by force, so it carries a negative tone. Sneaking into someone's house or building is '침입하다'. The side that gets attacked says '침략을 당하다' or '침략당하다'.

examples.ko: 월급이 밀린 판국에 보너스는 꿈도 못 꿔요.
examples.en: With our pay overdue, we can't even dream of a bonus.
You're bringing up a trip in a situation like this?

examples.ko: 나라 경제가 어려운 판국이라 모두 조심해요.
examples.en: The national economy is in a tough spot, so everyone is careful.

examples.ko: 시험이 내일인 판국에 게임이 하고 싶어요?
examples.en: The exam is tomorrow and you want to play games?

examples.ko: 일이 이런 판국이 될 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I didn't know things would end up in a state like this.

examples.ko: 판국을 보니 오늘은 일찍 퇴근하기 힘들겠어요.
examples.en: Looking at how things stand, leaving early today will be hard.

explain: '상황'과 비슷하지만 좋지 않은 일이 벌어진 형편에 주로 써요. '~ㄴ 판국에'로 많이 쓰고, 한숨이나 나무라는 느낌이 들어가요. 좋은 상황에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '상황' but is mostly used for a bad or troubling state of affairs. It often appears as '~ㄴ 판국에' and carries a sigh or a scolding tone. It is rarely used for good situations.

examples.ko: 회사는 재판에서 패소해서 큰돈을 물어 줬어요.
examples.en: The company lost the trial and had to pay a large sum.
He lost in the first trial but decided to go to court again.

examples.ko: 가게 주인은 소송에서 패소할까 봐 걱정했어요.
examples.en: The shop owner was worried about losing the lawsuit.
If I lose the case, do I have to pay the legal costs too?
The lawyer said there is a high chance of losing the case.

examples.ko: 그는 두 번이나 패소하고도 포기하지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even after losing twice, he did not give up.

explain: 반대말은 '승소하다'예요. 보통 '재판에서/소송에서 패소하다'로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '소송에서 지다'라고도 해요. 법정이나 뉴스 같은 상황에만 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '승소하다' (win a case). It is usually used as '재판에서/소송에서 패소하다', and in everyday talk people also say '소송에서 지다'. It only appears in court or news contexts.

examples.en: The prosecutor did not accept the ruling and appealed.
The result felt unfair, so I decided to appeal.
To appeal, you have to submit the documents first.
The company will appeal within a week.
A person who has appealed goes through the trial again.
Even if you appeal, the result may be the same.

explain: 1심 판결에 불복할 때 '항소하다'를 쓰고, 2심 뒤에 대법원으로 가는 건 '상고하다'예요. 보통 '판결에 항소하다'처럼 써요. 뉴스에서 '항소했다'로 자주 들려요.
explain_en: You 항소하다 when you do not accept a first-trial ruling; going to the Supreme Court after the second trial is 상고하다. It is used like '판결에 항소하다'. In the news you often hear '항소했다'.
